dataset.name: Light response (AQ) gas exchange by leaf age, Feb2017, PA-SLZ: Panama
description: Light response (AQ curves) gas exchange of sunlit canopy leaves of Terminalia amazonia (TERMAM), Vochysia ferruginea (VOCHFE), Miconia borealis (MICOBO) and Guatteria dumetorum (GUATDU) species from the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI) canopy crane site in the San Lorenzo National Park, Republic of Panama (PA-SLZ), during February 2017. Light response was measured on young, mature and old leaves collected before dawn on 3 days. The data package comprises a single data spreadsheet (*.xlsx), two metadata spreadsheets, and data collection protocols and workflow (*.pdf). This data was collected as part of the 2017 Brookhaven National Lab – Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute leaf traits by age campaign. See related datasets for further sample details, leaf water potential, leaf spectra, diurnal gas exchange, sap flow, leaf mass area (LMA) and leaf chemistry.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

Acknowledgement: This research was supported as part of NGEE-Tropics, funded by the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Biological and Environmental Research under contract no. DE-SC0012704.

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (Fort Sherman). Site ID: PA-SLZ. Located in Panama. Established in 1997, the FTS canopy crane is located approximately 11km South West from the city of Colon, in the middle theParque Natural San Lorenzo (formerly known as FortSherman) and is surrounded by 300-year old, low-landtropical rainforest. The crane is 52 meters tall with aradius of 54 meters, and can reach approximately 240species of trees and lianas.
